source.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י גְאַלְתִּ֔יךָ קָרָ֥אתִי בְשִׁמְךָ֖ לִי־אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now thus says Yahweh, [who] created you, Jacob, and [who] formed you, Israel: do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you; I have called by your name; to me you [are].

en.L: And now thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [the one who] created you, O Jacob, and [the one who] formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called [you] by your name; you [are] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.
en.B: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Creator, Jacob, the one who shaped you, Israel, says this: Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I called you by your own name; you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} speaks, the one who created you, Jacob, and shaped you, Israel. He says: Do not be afraid. I have bought you back. I have called you by name. You belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: I have redeemed you: I have bought you back as a near relative would
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of a relative who pays to free a family member or win back lost family land (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49). God acts as Israel's next of kin; the past form speaks of the rescue as already done. The same root gives the title Redeemer (43:14; 41:14).

decisions.choice: created, formed: God made Israel as he made the world and the first human
decisions.reason: The verbs are those of Genesis 1:1 and 2:7. Here they describe God bringing Jacob's family into being as his people (43:7, 21; 44:2).

decisions.choice: I have called you by your name: I have claimed you personally as my own
decisions.reason: To call someone by name is to single them out and claim them (40:26; 45:3-4). The last words, literally "to me you", state the result: Israel belongs to God.

decisions.choice: I have bought you back
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what redeeming means; Literal and Balanced keep "redeemed" to match the title Redeemer.

source.text: כִּֽי־תַעֲבֹ֤ר בַּמַּ֨יִם֙ אִתְּךָ־אָ֔נִי וּבַנְּהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּךָ כִּֽי־תֵלֵ֤ךְ בְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶ֔ה וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר־בָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you pass through the waters, with you I [will be]; and through the rivers, they will not overflow you; when you walk in fire, you will not be scorched, and flame will not burn in you.

en.L: When you pass through the waters, with you I [will be]; and through the rivers, they will not overflow you; when you walk in fire, you will not be scorched, and [the] flame will not burn you.
en.B: When you go through the waters, I will be beside you; through the rivers, they will not flood over you. When you walk in the fire, you will not be scorched; the flame will not burn you up.
en.R: You will go through deep water, but I will be with you. You will cross rivers, but they will not carry you away. You will walk in fire, but it will not scorch you. The flames will not harm you.

decisions.choice: waters and rivers: dangers like those Israel passed through at the sea and the Jordan
decisions.reason: The picture recalls the crossing of the sea (Exodus 14) and of the Jordan (Joshua 3), which verses 16-17 bring to mind again. Water and fire together stand for every kind of danger (Psalm 66:12).

decisions.choice: when you pass ... when you walk: the trials will come, and God will be there in them
decisions.reason: The word can mean "when" or "if". The promise is not that Israel will avoid danger but that God will be present in it (Daniel 3:25).

decisions.choice: You will go ... but I will be with you
decisions.reason: Readable turns each "when" clause into its own sentence and joins the promise with "but".

source.text: כִּ֗י אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ נָתַ֤תִּי כָפְרְךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם כּ֥וּשׁ וּסְבָ֖א תַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For I [am] Yahweh your God, [the] Holy One of Israel, your deliverer; I have given [as] your ransom Egypt, Cush and Seba in your place.

en.L: For I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I have given [as] your ransom Egypt, Cush and Seba in your place.
en.B: For I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; I am the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I have given Egypt as the price of your freedom, Cush and Seba in exchange for you.
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, the Holy One of Israel, who saves you. I have given up Egypt, Cush, and Seba in exchange for you. They are the price of your freedom.

decisions.choice: ransom: the price paid to set a life free
decisions.reason: The word is used of a payment that frees a person whose life is forfeit (Exodus 21:30; 30:12). God pictures himself giving up other nations so that Israel may go free (verse 4).

decisions.choice: Egypt, Cush and Seba: the great lands of the far south
decisions.reason: Cush was the kingdom on the Nile south of Egypt; Seba is a people listed with Cush (Genesis 10:7; Psalm 72:10; 45:14). The picture may look to the Persian empire, which freed the exiles and later took Egypt itself (525 BC), but the verse does not name who receives the ransom.

decisions.choice: your Savior: the one who rescues you
decisions.reason: The word means one who delivers from danger or an enemy. In this chapter only the LORD is Savior (43:11; 45:21).

decisions.choice: They are the price of your freedom.
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ransom" in a separate sentence.

source.text: מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקַ֧רְתָּ בְעֵינַ֛י נִכְבַּ֖דְתָּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֲהַבְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֶתֵּ֤ן אָדָם֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים תַּ֥חַת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because you are precious in my eyes, you are honored, and I love you; and I give humankind in your place and peoples in place of your life.

en.L: Because you are precious in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, you are honored, and I, I love you; and I give people in your place and peoples in place of your life.
en.B: You are dear in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight; you are held in honor, and I love you. So I will hand over human lives for you, whole peoples for your life.
en.R: You are worth a great deal to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are honored, and I love you. So I will give other people in your place. I will give up nations to save your life.

decisions.choice: because you are precious ... honored ... loved: the reasons for the ransom
decisions.reason: The verse gives God's reasons for the exchange in verse 3. The pronoun "I" is written out before "love you", stressing that it is God himself who loves Israel (Deuteronomy 7:7-8).

decisions.choice: humankind: other human beings, not one named nation
decisions.reason: The word is the general term for human beings. It widens the list of verse 3: God will give up others, whoever they may be, for Israel's sake.

source.text: אַל־תִּירָ֖א כִּ֣י אִתְּךָ־אָ֑נִי מִמִּזְרָח֙ אָבִ֣יא זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֖ב אֲקַבְּצֶֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be afraid, for with you I [am]; from [the] east I will bring your offspring, and from [the] west I will gather you.

en.L: Do not fear, for with you I [am]; from [the] east I will bring your offspring, and from [the] west I will gather you.
en.B: Do not be afraid, for I am at your side. From the east I will lead your descendants back; from the west I will gather you in.
en.R: Do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bring your descendants back from lands in the east. I will gather you from lands in the west.

decisions.choice: from the east ... from the west: the scattered people brought home from every direction
decisions.reason: Verses 5-6 name all four directions: God will gather his people from wherever they have been scattered (11:12; Deuteronomy 30:3-4).

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: the command of verse 1 repeated
decisions.reason: The repeated command frames verses 1-7. The reason is again God's presence (verse 2).

decisions.choice: lands in the east; lands in the west
decisions.reason: Readable says that the directions refer to the lands where the people are scattered.

source.text: אֹמַ֤ר לַצָּפוֹן֙ תֵּ֔נִי וּלְתֵימָ֖ן אַל־תִּכְלָ֑אִי הָבִ֤יאִי בָנַי֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וּבְנוֹתַ֖י מִקְצֵ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: I will say to the north, give, and to the south, do not hold back; bring my sons from afar and my daughters from [the] end of the earth,

en.L: I will say to the north, "Give [them up]," and to the south, "Do not hold [them] back; bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sons from afar and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} daughters from the end of the earth,
en.B: I will tell the north, "Release them!" and the south, "Do not keep them back! Bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sons from far away, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} daughters from the farthest edge of the earth,
en.R: I will command the north, "Let them go!" I will tell the south, "Do not keep them! Bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sons from far away. Bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} daughters from the most distant places on earth.

decisions.choice: give, do not hold back, bring: commands to the north and the south, running on into verse 7
decisions.reason: The commands are addressed to the north and the south as if they were people holding Israel captive. The command "bring" continues to the end of verse 7.

decisions.choice: my sons and my daughters: the whole people, as God's own children
decisions.reason: God calls the exiles his children (1:2; Exodus 4:22). Naming daughters as well as sons makes clear that every one of them is meant.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: The commands have no object; the context shows that the captives are meant.

source.text: כֹּ֚ל הַנִּקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֔י וְלִכְבוֹדִ֖י בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף־עֲשִׂיתִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: everyone called by my name, and for my glory I created him, I formed him, also I made him.

en.L: everyone [who is] called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory I created him; I formed him; yes, I made him."
en.B: all who are called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, each one I created for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory, each one I formed, yes, each one I made."
en.R: Bring everyone who belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the people I created to show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory. I formed them. I made them."

decisions.choice: called by my name: belonging to me
decisions.reason: A people or place called by someone's name is owned by them (63:19; Deuteronomy 28:10; Amos 9:12).

decisions.choice: for my glory: so that God's greatness would be seen through them
decisions.reason: Israel exists to make God's glory known (43:21; 49:3).

decisions.choice: created, formed, made: three verbs for one act, building to a climax
decisions.reason: The verbs gather up the language of verse 1 and Genesis 1-2. The word "also" before the last gives it extra weight.

decisions.choice: everyone who belongs to me; to show my glory
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom and the purpose, and repeats "Bring" from verse 6 because it starts a new sentence.

source.text: הוֹצִ֥יא עַם־עִוֵּ֖ר וְעֵינַ֣יִם יֵ֑שׁ וְחֵרְשִׁ֖ים וְאָזְנַ֥יִם לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Bring out a people blind, and eyes there are, and deaf, and ears [belong] to them.

en.L: Bring out [the] people [who are] blind, yet eyes there are, and [the] deaf, yet ears [belong] to them.
en.B: Bring out the blind people who have eyes, the deaf who have ears.
en.R: Bring {my} people out to the court. They are blind, though they have eyes. They are deaf, though they have ears.

decisions.choice: bring out: a call to bring the people into court
decisions.reason: The verb form can be read as a command or as a past statement ("he has brought out"). The court scene of verse 9 favors a summons. Who is to bring them out is not said.

decisions.choice: blind and deaf: Israel, which has eyes and ears but does not understand
decisions.reason: Israel is the blind and deaf servant of 42:18-20 (6:9-10). Yet these same people are called as God's witnesses (verse 10).

decisions.choice: my people; to the court
decisions.reason: Readable names who is brought out and where; verses 9-10 show the setting is a trial and the people are Israel.

source.text: כָּֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו וְיֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ לְאֻמִּ֔ים מִ֤י בָהֶם֙ יַגִּ֣יד זֹ֔את וְרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת יַשְׁמִיעֻ֑נוּ יִתְּנ֤וּ עֵֽדֵיהֶם֙ וְיִצְדָּ֔קוּ וְיִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְיֹאמְר֥וּ אֱמֶֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: All the nations have gathered together, and peoples assemble; who among them will declare this, and former [things] cause us to hear? Let them give their witnesses and be justified, and let them hear and say, truth.

en.L: All the nations have assembled together, and [the] peoples gather; who among them can declare this, and make us hear the former things? Let them present their witnesses and be proved right, and let them hear and say, "Truth."
en.B: All the nations are gathered together; the peoples have assembled. Which of them could announce this, or make us hear the former things? Let them produce their witnesses and be shown to be in the right; let people hear them and say, "It is the truth."
en.R: All the nations have come together. The peoples have gathered. Can any of their gods tell what will happen? Can any of them tell us what they foretold long ago? Let them bring witnesses to show they are right. Then people will hear and say, "That is the truth."

decisions.choice: a court case: the nations and their gods are summoned to prove their claims
decisions.reason: As in 41:1 and 41:21-24, the scene is a lawsuit. The nations must bring witnesses that their gods foretold events; Israel is God's witness (verse 10).

decisions.choice: this; the former things: events foretold before they happened
decisions.reason: "The former things" are earlier events that were announced in advance and came true (41:22; 42:9; 46:9). "This" is the rescue now being announced.

decisions.choice: let them hear and say: those who hear the evidence, possibly the witnesses themselves
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It may be anyone who hears the case, or the witnesses, who would have to admit what is true.

decisions.choice: any of their gods
decisions.reason: Readable names the gods behind the nations; the challenge is to the idols, as in 41:21-24.

source.text: אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְעַבְדִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחָ֑רְתִּי לְמַ֣עַן תֵּ֠דְעוּ וְתַאֲמִ֨ינוּ לִ֤י וְתָבִ֨ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא לְפָנַי֙ לֹא־נ֣וֹצַר אֵ֔ל וְאַחֲרַ֖י לֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: You [are] my witnesses, declares Yahweh, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I [am] he; before me no god was formed, and after me there will not be.

en.L: You [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and understand that I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}: before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no god was formed, and after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} there will be none.
en.B: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, the one I have chosen, so that you will come to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, put your trust in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and grasp that I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}. Before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no god was ever shaped, and none will come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, the one I chose. I chose you so that you would know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I want you to understand that I alone am God. No god was made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and there will be none after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: you are my witnesses: Israel's own history is the evidence in the trial
decisions.reason: The nations cannot produce witnesses (verse 9), but Israel has seen God announce events and then bring them about (43:12; 44:8).

decisions.choice: my servant: Israel, the same "you" who are the witnesses
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes the witnesses themselves, as Israel is called God's chosen servant in 41:8 and 44:1. It could instead name a separate servant figure (42:1) beside Israel.

decisions.choice: I am he: I am the one who is God, the same from first to last
decisions.reason: The short phrase is God's claim to be the only true God, who stays the same and is present in all events (41:4; 43:13; 46:4; 48:12; Deuteronomy 32:39). Jesus uses the same words in Greek in John 8:24, 28; 13:19.

decisions.choice: no god was formed: idols are made, but God was not
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of craftsmen who form idols (44:9-10). No god came before the LORD or will come after him.

decisions.choice: I alone am God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "I am he" from the rest of the verse; Literal and Balanced keep the short phrase.

decisions.choice: The LORD says: ... I chose you
decisions.reason: Readable moves "declares the LORD" to the start and repeats "I chose you" to begin a new sentence.

source.text: אָנֹכִ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין מִבַּלְעָדַ֖י מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: I, I [am] Yahweh, and there is not besides me a savior.

en.L: I, I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and apart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} there is no savior.
en.B: It is I, I who am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; there is no savior but {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I, yes I, am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. No one but {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} can save you.

decisions.choice: I, I: the pronoun doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Doubling the pronoun stresses that God alone is the one speaking and acting (43:25; 48:15; 51:12).

decisions.choice: no savior besides me: only the LORD can rescue
decisions.reason: The idols cannot save (45:20); the LORD is the only Savior (45:21; Hosea 13:4).

decisions.choice: can save you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun into a verb and supplies the object.

source.text: אָנֹכִ֞י הִגַּ֤דְתִּי וְהוֹשַׁ֨עְתִּי֙ וְהִשְׁמַ֔עְתִּי וְאֵ֥ין בָּכֶ֖ם זָ֑ר וְאַתֶּ֥ם עֵדַ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽאֲנִי־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: I have declared and I have saved and I have proclaimed, and there was not among you a strange [god]; and you [are] my witnesses, declares Yahweh, and I [am] God.

en.L: I declared, and I saved, and I proclaimed, and there was no strange [god] among you; and you [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I [am] God.
en.B: It was I who told it beforehand, I who saved, I who made it heard; no foreign god was among you. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I am God.
en.R: I told you what would happen. Then I saved you, and I made it known. No strange god among you did this. You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witnesses, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am God.

decisions.choice: declared, saved, proclaimed: God announced the rescue, carried it out, and made it known
decisions.reason: The order matters: God foretold, then acted, so the outcome proves the claim. The idols cannot do this (41:22-23).

decisions.choice: a strange god: a foreign god Israel had taken up
decisions.reason: The word means foreign or strange; used alone it can mean a foreign god (Deuteronomy 32:16; Psalm 81:10). The point is that no such god did these things.

decisions.choice: god
decisions.reason: Supplied: the context is God against the idols.

source.text: גַּם־מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְאֵ֥ין מִיָּדִ֖י מַצִּ֑יל אֶפְעַ֖ל וּמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Also from [the] day I [am] he, and there is no one from my hand delivering; I act, and who will turn it back?

en.L: Also from [the] day I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, and there is no one delivering from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand; I act, and who will reverse it?
en.B: From the first day on, I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; there is no one who can rescue from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power. I work, and who can undo it?
en.R: From the beginning of time I have been God. No one can rescue anyone from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power. When I do something, no one can undo it.

decisions.choice: from the day: from the first day, since time began
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean from the first day there was, or from this day on. The theme of God being first and last (41:4; 44:6) favors the first.

decisions.choice: from my hand: out of my power
decisions.reason: The line echoes Deuteronomy 32:39 almost word for word.

decisions.choice: who will turn it back: no one can reverse what God does
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of God's stretched-out hand in 14:27.

decisions.choice: I have been God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "I am he" as in verse 10.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְמַעַנְכֶ֞ם שִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי בָבֶ֗לָה וְהוֹרַדְתִּ֤י בָֽרִיחִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וְכַשְׂדִּ֖ים בָּאֳנִיּ֥וֹת רִנָּתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, your redeemer, [the] Holy One of Israel: for your sake I have sent to Babylon, and I will bring down fugitives all of them, and [the] Chaldeans in the ships of their shout.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and I will bring down all of them [as] fugitives, and the Chaldeans in the ships of their rejoicing.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says this: For your sake I have sent an enemy against Babylon. I will bring all of them down in flight, the Chaldeans, in the ships that once rang with their shouts.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: To help you, I will send an enemy army against Babylon. I will make all the Babylonians run away. They will run for their lives in the ships that used to fill them with joy.

decisions.choice: fugitives: people fleeing
decisions.reason: The word can mean fugitives or the bars of a city's gates (45:2). With "bring down" and "all of them" it most likely describes the Babylonians fleeing; "I will bring down all the bars" is also possible.

decisions.choice: in the ships of their shout: the ships they once cheered now carry them in flight
alternatives: their shouting turns to lament in the ships
decisions.reason: Babylon's trade moved on its rivers and canals. The phrase probably means the ships in which they rejoiced; it could also mean their shouts of joy turn to cries in the ships. The verse is difficult.

decisions.choice: I have sent: God sends a conqueror; the Chaldeans are the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The one sent is not named here; 45:1-4 names Cyrus, whose army took Babylon in 539 BC. The Chaldeans were the people who ruled Babylon (13:19).

decisions.choice: an enemy (army)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; Balanced and Readable supply who is sent.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: Readable uses the settled name for the Chaldeans.

source.text: אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה קְדֽוֹשְׁכֶ֑ם בּוֹרֵ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מַלְכְּכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: I [am] Yahweh, your Holy One, creator of Israel, your king.

en.L: I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Holy One, [the] Creator of Israel, your King.
en.B: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Holy One, who created Israel, your King.
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your holy God. I created Israel, and I am your King.

decisions.choice: your King: the LORD is Israel's true king
decisions.reason: God is called king of his people in 6:5, 33:22, 41:21 and 44:6. With Israel's kings gone, God still rules and rescues them.

decisions.choice: creator of Israel: the one who brought Israel into being
decisions.reason: The word is the same as in verse 1; God made Israel a people.

decisions.choice: your holy God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title "your Holy One".

source.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ וּבְמַ֥יִם עַזִּ֖ים נְתִיבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, who makes in [the] sea a way, and in mighty waters a path,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one making a way in the sea, and in mighty waters a path,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this, the one who makes a road through the sea, a path through surging waters,
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. He is the one who made a road through the sea, a path through the powerful waters.

decisions.choice: a way in the sea: the crossing of the sea at the exodus
decisions.reason: The words recall how God led Israel through the sea (Exodus 14:21-29; Psalm 77:20). Verse 19 will promise a new way, through the wilderness.

decisions.choice: the one making: a description of God
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle, describing God by what he did at the exodus and still can do.

decisions.choice: He is the one who made
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and puts the description in the past, since it recalls the exodus.

source.text: הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב־וָס֖וּס חַ֣יִל וְעִזּ֑וּז יַחְדָּ֤ו יִשְׁכְּבוּ֙ בַּל־יָק֔וּמוּ דָּעֲכ֖וּ כַּפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה כָבֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: who brings out chariot and horse, army and strong [one] together; they lie down, they will not rise; they are extinguished, like the wick they are quenched:

en.L: the one bringing out chariot and horse, army and mighty [one] together; they lie down, they will not rise; they are extinguished; like the wick they are put out:
en.B: who brought out chariot and horse, army and warrior together: they lay down and did not get up; they went out, quenched like a wick:
en.R: He brought out chariots and horses and a powerful army. They all fell down together and never got up again. They died out like the flame of a lamp that is put out. He says:

decisions.choice: chariot and horse ... they lie down, they will not rise: Pharaoh's army drowned in the sea
decisions.reason: God drew Egypt's chariots after Israel into the sea, where they perished (Exodus 14:23-28; 15:4-5).

decisions.choice: like a wick they are put out: their life ended as easily as a lamp is snuffed
decisions.reason: A wick is the cord of a small oil lamp. The same picture is used of the gentle servant in 42:3, who will not put out a dim wick.

decisions.choice: the flame of a lamp; He says:
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wick and repeats "He says" because verses 16-17 were broken into separate sentences.

source.text: אַֽל־תִּזְכְּר֖וּ רִֽאשֹׁנ֑וֹת וְקַדְמֹנִיּ֖וֹת אַל־תִּתְבֹּנָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not remember former [things], and ancient [things] do not consider.

en.L: Do not remember [the] former things, and the things of old do not consider.
en.B: Do not call to mind the former things, or brood over the things of long ago.
en.R: Do not keep thinking about what I did in the past. Do not keep looking back at long ago.

decisions.choice: the former things: God's earlier saving acts, even the exodus just described
decisions.reason: Here the phrase points back to verses 16-17. Israel is not told to forget the exodus but that what God is about to do will outshine it (verse 19). Some take it as Israel's past troubles instead.

decisions.choice: what I did in the past
decisions.reason: Readable names the former things as God's acts, following the meaning decision.

source.text: הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ עַתָּ֣ה תִצְמָ֔ח הֲל֖וֹא תֵֽדָע֑וּהָ אַ֣ף אָשִׂ֤ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֔רֶךְ בִּֽישִׁמ֖וֹן נְהָרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I [am] doing a new [thing]; now it sprouts; will you not know it? Also I will make in the wilderness a way, in [the] desert rivers.

en.L: Look, I [am] doing a new thing; now it springs up; do you not know it? Yes, I will make a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert.
en.B: See, I am about to do something new; even now it is sprouting. Do you not recognize it? I will cut a road through the wilderness and make rivers flow in the barren land.
en.R: Watch! I am going to do something new. It is starting to happen right now, like a plant breaking out of the ground. Can you not see it? I will make a road through the desert. I will make rivers flow in the dry land.

decisions.choice: a new thing: a new exodus, the return from exile
decisions.reason: God will lead his people home through the wilderness as he once led them through the sea, in a way that surpasses the first (42:9; 48:6; 52:12).

decisions.choice: it sprouts: it is already beginning, like a shoot breaking the ground
decisions.reason: The verb is used of plants coming up (42:9; 44:4). The phrase "Look, I am doing" can describe something happening now or about to happen.

decisions.choice: rivers: the Masoretic Text
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "paths" here, matching "a way" in the line before. The Masoretic reading "rivers" matches verse 20.

decisions.choice: like a plant breaking out of the ground
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture in the verb "sprout".

source.text: תְּכַבְּדֵ֨נִי֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה תַּנִּ֖ים וּבְנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה כִּֽי־נָתַ֨תִּי בַמִּדְבָּ֜ר מַ֗יִם נְהָרוֹת֙ בִּֽישִׁימֹ֔ן לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת עַמִּ֥י בְחִירִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: It will honor me, the animal of the field, jackals and daughters of ostrich, for I have given in the wilderness water, rivers in [the] desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,

en.L: The animals of the field will honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, jackals and ostriches, for I have put water in the wilderness, rivers in [the] desert, to give drink to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} chosen,
en.B: Even the wild beasts will honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the jackals and the ostriches, because I have put water in the wilderness, rivers in the barren land, to give drink to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} chosen ones,
en.R: Wild animals will honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even jackals and ostriches, because I have put water in the desert and rivers in the dry land. I did this to give water to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the ones I chose.

decisions.choice: daughters of the ostrich: ostriches
decisions.reason: "Daughters of" is a way of naming members of a kind. The bird lives in desert places; some take it as the owl (13:21; 34:13).

decisions.choice: the wild animals honor God: the whole land benefits when God provides for his people
decisions.reason: The desert creatures share the water and so give God honor (41:17-20; Joel 1:20).

decisions.choice: my chosen: Israel, whom God chose
decisions.reason: Israel is God's chosen one in 41:8-9; 44:1; 45:4.

decisions.choice: ostriches
decisions.reason: The idiom "daughters of the ostrich" is rendered by the plain name of the bird.

source.text: עַם־זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: a people this I formed for myself; my praise they will recount.

en.L: the people whom I formed for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}; they will recount {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} praise.
en.B: the people I formed to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own; they will recount {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} praises.
en.R: I made these people for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. They will tell everyone how great I am.

decisions.choice: my praise: the deeds for which God is praised
decisions.reason: The word means praise and also the praiseworthy acts that call it out (42:8; 63:7; Psalm 78:4). Israel will tell the story of what God has done.

decisions.choice: this people whom I formed: the people of verse 20, now described
decisions.reason: A short poetic relative word links this line to "my people, my chosen" in verse 20.

decisions.choice: tell everyone how great I am
decisions.reason: Readable explains what recounting God's praise means.

source.text: וְלֹא־אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּֽי־יָגַ֥עְתָּ בִּ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And not me you have called, Jacob, for you have grown weary of me, Israel.

en.L: And not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} have you called, O Jacob, for you have grown weary of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, O Israel.
en.B: Yet it was not on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that you called, Jacob; you have grown tired of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Israel.
en.R: But you, people of Jacob, have not prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. People of Israel, you have become tired of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: call on: pray to and worship
decisions.reason: To call on God is to turn to him in prayer and worship (55:6; Psalm 50:15). The object "me" comes first, stressing that it was not the LORD they called on.

decisions.choice: you have grown weary of me: Israel tired of God
alternatives: nor have you wearied yourself for me
decisions.reason: The words can mean that Israel grew tired of God, or, carrying over the "not", that Israel did not trouble itself for him. Verses 23-24 play on the same verb: God did not weary Israel, but Israel wearied God.

decisions.choice: people of Jacob; People of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Jacob and Israel are the people.

source.text: לֹֽא־הֵבֵ֤יאתָ לִּי֙ שֵׂ֣ה עֹלֹתֶ֔יךָ וּזְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א כִבַּדְתָּ֑נִי לֹ֤א הֶעֱבַדְתִּ֨יךָ֙ בְּמִנְחָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הוֹגַעְתִּ֖יךָ בִּלְבוֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you have brought to me the sheep of your burnt offerings, and [with] your sacrifices not you have honored me; not I have burdened you with offering, and not I have wearied you with frankincense.

en.L: You have not brought {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the sheep of your burnt offerings, and with your sacrifices you have not honored {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; I have not burdened you with grain offerings, and I have not wearied you with frankincense.
en.B: No sheep for burnt offerings have you brought {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; with your sacrifices you have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no honor. I laid no burden of grain offerings on you; I did not make you weary for the sake of frankincense.
en.R: You did not bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sheep to burn as offerings. You did not honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with your sacrifices. I did not make you work hard to bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} grain offerings. I did not wear you out by asking for sweet-smelling incense.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, grain offerings, frankincense: the regular offerings of worship
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar; a grain offering of flour and oil was often burned with frankincense, a fragrant resin (Leviticus 1; 2:1-2).

decisions.choice: you have not brought me: Israel's worship did not truly reach God
alternatives: in exile they could not sacrifice
decisions.reason: This may mean that in exile no sacrifices could be offered, or that the sacrifices Israel did offer were not really for God (1:11-15; Amos 5:25). Either way, God has not been demanding.

decisions.choice: burdened ... wearied: made you labor ... tired you out
decisions.reason: The first verb is the one for serving as a slave. God did not make Israel slave for him; verse 24 turns both verbs around.

source.text: לֹא־קָנִ֨יתָ לִּ֤י בַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ קָנֶ֔ה וְחֵ֥לֶב זְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א הִרְוִיתָ֑נִי אַ֗ךְ הֶעֱבַדְתַּ֨נִי֙ בְּחַטֹּאותֶ֔יךָ הוֹגַעְתַּ֖נִי בַּעֲוֺנֹתֶֽיךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not you have bought for me with money calamus, and [with] the fat of your sacrifices not you have satisfied me; but you have burdened me with your sins, you have wearied me with your iniquities.

en.L: You have not bought {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sweet cane with money, and with the fat of your sacrifices you have not satisfied {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; rather, you have burdened {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with your sins; you have wearied {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with your iniquities.
en.B: You have not spent silver to buy {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fragrant cane or filled {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead you have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} toil like a slave under your sins and worn {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} out with your guilt.
en.R: You did not spend money to buy {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sweet-smelling cane. You did not satisfy {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead, your sins have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} work like a slave. Your many sins have worn {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} out.

decisions.choice: calamus; the fat: costly cane for incense and oil, and the best part of a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Calamus, or sweet cane, was an imported spice used in the holy anointing oil (Exodus 30:23; Jeremiah 6:20). The fat of a sacrifice belonged to God and was burned (Leviticus 3:16).

decisions.choice: you have burdened me: you have made me serve like a slave
decisions.reason: The verbs repeat those of verse 23, turned around: God did not make Israel his slave, but Israel's sins made God labor under them (compare 53:11-12).

decisions.choice: toil like a slave; work like a slave
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of slave labor; Literal keeps "burdened".

source.text: אָנֹכִ֨י אָנֹכִ֥י ה֛וּא מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖יךָ לְמַעֲנִ֑י וְחַטֹּאתֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶזְכֹּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: I, I [am] he [who] wipes out your transgressions for my sake, and your sins I will not remember.

en.L: I, I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [who] wipes out your transgressions for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} [own] sake, and your sins I will not remember.
en.B: I, yes I, am the one who wipes out your rebellious acts for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own sake; your sins I will not keep in mind.
en.R: I, yes I, am the one who wipes away your rebellion against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I do it for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own sake. I will not hold your sins against you.

decisions.choice: wipes out: erases, as writing is wiped from a record
decisions.reason: The verb is used of blotting out names or records (Exodus 32:32-33; Psalm 51:3). God removes the record of Israel's rebellions.

decisions.choice: for my own sake: because of who God is, not because Israel deserves it
decisions.reason: God forgives to honor his own name and character (48:9-11; Ezekiel 36:22). The verse follows directly on Israel's failure in verses 22-24.

decisions.choice: I will not remember: I will not hold your sins against you
decisions.reason: When God does not remember sins, he no longer acts on them (64:8; Jeremiah 31:34).

decisions.choice: am the one who
decisions.reason: Here "he" joins the pronoun to the verb that follows: "I am the one who wipes out".

decisions.choice: I will not hold your sins against you
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

source.text: הַזְכִּירֵ֕נִי נִשָּׁפְטָ֖ה יָ֑חַד סַפֵּ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה לְמַ֥עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Cause me to remember; let us go into judgment together; recount, you, so that you may be justified.

en.L: Remind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; let us go to judgment together; recount [your case], you, so that you may be proved right.
en.B: Remind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; let us take this to court together. Lay out your account, so that you may be declared in the right.
en.R: Remind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} of your case, if you can. Let us go to court together. Tell your side, and try to prove that you are innocent.

decisions.choice: let us go into judgment together: a court case between God and Israel
decisions.reason: God calls Israel to argue its case, as in 1:18 and 41:1.

decisions.choice: remind me ... so that you may be proved right: an ironic challenge
decisions.reason: Having just said that he forgives for his own sake (verse 25), God invites Israel to show any merit it has. Verse 27 shows it has none.

decisions.choice: if you can; try to
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the challenge in God's words.

source.text: אָבִ֥יךָ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן חָטָ֑א וּמְלִיצֶ֖יךָ פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Your father, the first, sinned, and your interpreters rebelled against me.

en.L: Your first father sinned, and your spokesmen rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Your earliest ancestor sinned, and those who spoke for you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Your very first ancestor sinned. Your leaders who spoke for you turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: your first father: probably Jacob, the father of the nation
decisions.reason: The chapter addresses the people as Jacob (verses 22, 28), and Hosea 12:3-5 recalls Jacob's wrongdoing. Others take it as Abraham (51:2) or Adam.

decisions.choice: your spokesmen: those who stood between the people and God
decisions.reason: The word means an interpreter or go-between (Genesis 42:23; 2 Chronicles 32:31). It probably means Israel's priests, prophets and leaders.

source.text: וַאֲחַלֵּ֖ל שָׂ֣רֵי קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לַחֵ֨רֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְגִדּוּפִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will profane officials of holiness, and I will give to destruction Jacob and Israel to reviling.

en.L: So I profaned [the] officials of [the] sanctuary, and I gave Jacob to destruction, and Israel to reviling.
en.B: So I treated the leaders of the sanctuary as unholy; I handed Jacob over to be destroyed and Israel to be mocked.
en.R: So I took away the holy rank of the temple leaders. I handed the people of Jacob over to destruction, and I let others insult the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: I profaned, I gave: the judgment of the exile, already carried out
alternatives: I will profane ... I will give
decisions.reason: The verb forms most likely tell what God has done: the fall of Jerusalem and the exile. They can also be read as future ("I will profane").

decisions.choice: officials of the sanctuary: the priests and leaders of the temple
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the priestly officers in 1 Chronicles 24:5. To profane them is to strip them of their holy status.

decisions.choice: destruction: the ban, being given over wholly to destruction
decisions.reason: The word is used of what is devoted to God by being destroyed (Joshua 6:17; 34:2). The ban once laid on Israel's enemies has fallen on Israel itself.

decisions.choice: I let others insult
decisions.reason: Readable supplies who does the reviling.
